newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia requests extradition of hijackers.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia requests extradition of hijackers.

text.p: Ethiopia on Monday asked the government of Comoro Islands to extradite two Ethiopian hijackers of the Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961 which crashed off the Indian Ocean islands on Saturday.

Prime Minister Meles Zenawi thanked the Comorans for their "prompt and exceptional" rescue effort and said: "The Comoros would take appropriate and prompt action in handing over the perpetrators of this heinous crime to Ethiopia (for trial)."
"The response to the disaster was characteristic of the brotherhood prevailing among the countries of Africa," Meles said in the message issued in Ethiopia's capital Addis Ababa.

Meles said Ethiopia was "fully satisfied" that Comoran authorities and citizens did all in their power to save the lives of the Flight 961 passengers. Meles also specifically thanked the French authorities for their help.
The airline had said it will issue a list of all survivors and the dead on Monday. It had earlier said that 52 people had survived out of 175 passengers and crew who were on board the Boeing 767.

Ethiopian government officials said Meles's request had been delivered to Comoran authorities but it was not immediately known when formal extradition pleas would be taken to court in the Indian Ocean islands' capital, Moroni.
Two of the three hijackers were known to have survived the crash. They are under detention in the Comoros.

After proper identification and prayers, the bodies will be transported to their respective destinations accompanied by airline officials. Ethiopia has declared a three-day mourning period starting on Monday and flags are flying at half-mast.
